paragraphs: In Kiddushin 24a he asks Rav Ashi, “But did Rami bar Yechezkel not teach…?” Hyman thinks he is probably Rav Shemen of Mesovra, mentioned in Chullin 18b and Niddah 36a. There Ravina tells Rav Ashi, “Rav Shemen of Mesovra told me: Mar Zutra visited our place,” etc. Hyman’s printed notice cites Dikdukei Soferim for the form מסיכרא [supplied כמסיכרא].

notes.text: The supplied form כמסיכרא has an initial kaf whose function is unresolved; it is not silently normalized to a different town-name. The identification with Mesovra remains Hyman’s tentative suggestion.

No new primary scalar or DikdukeiSoferim witness was supplied. The earlier Chullin search lead does not resolve initial kaf in כמסיכרא or license normalization to ממסיכרא, a modern town or an ethnic identity. Hyman’s close-to-say identification of the Kiddushin questioner with Shemen of Mesovra remains tentative. Full RavShemen/RavAshi/Ravina/MarZutra and the reporting direction are supplied; no new chronology or merged person follows.

Hyman’s printed citation is Kiddushin 24a. The consulted passage at 24b names Rav Shemen asking Rav Ashi about the teaching of Rami bar Yechezkel. In Chullin 18b, Ravina reports that Rav Shemen of Mesovra told him about Mar Zutra’s visit. Niddah 36a reads “told us,” gives the place as Sikhra, and reports a different ruling. Hyman’s printed notice and Dikdukei Soferim on Chullin 18b both give מסיכרא, beside the supplied transcription כמסיכרא. The apparatus also records a reading with “on one occasion.” The identification of the Kiddushin questioner with the Rav Shemen named in these parallels is Hyman’s suggestion.
